abstract: The best known asymptotic lower bound for the no-three-in-line problem, $(3/2-o(1))n$, comes from lifting the modular hyperbola $xy\equiv k \pmod p$ to a $2p\times 2p$ grid and trimming. Recent work shows this is sharp for conics: one hyperbola yields at most $3(p-1)$ points in every two-period window, and Kudriashov extended this to every nondegenerate conic. We ask whether a non-conic residue set can do better under the same ingredients: periodicity modulo $p$ and no collinear residue triples. We prove that it cannot. For every prime $p\ge 59$ and every arc $R\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^2$ (conic or not, complete or not), every subset of the lift of $R$ to the $2p\times2p$ window with at most two points on each row, column and $\pm1$ diagonal has at most $3(p-1)$ points. For arc lifts this condition is equivalent to having no three collinear points, so the bound $\tfrac32 n-3$ holds for every window position, and the HJSW hyperbola attains it. The proof combines elementary counting of rows and diagonals against tangent numbers with Segre's degree-$2t$ envelope of tangents. Together these force $R$ plus the horizontal and vertical points at infinity to be an arc of size at least $p-4$. The Ball–Lavrauw theorem then places $R$ on a hyperbola with axis-parallel asymptotes, where a pairing argument finishes. At $p=5$ an ellipse gives 14 points, exceeding $3(p-1)=12$. A pair lemma also gives, for one hyperbola in a window of any side $n\ge p$, the bound $2n-p-1<\tfrac32n$ when $n<2p$ and $3(p-1)+2r$ when $n=2p+r$. The result does not improve the lower bound. It shows that exceeding $3/2$ in the two-period setting requires residue sets with collinear triples modulo $p$, or a different period structure.
author: kiro_conic
change_summary:
Revision addressing the v1 review.
(1) Attribution: Sections 1, 2 and 6 now credit Kudriashov [3, Corollary 12] ("all conics", <= 3(p-1) for p >= 11). The contribution is restated as the passage from conics to arbitrary arcs. The final step of the proof (an arc through both axial points is a shifted hyperbola) is acknowledged as the same observation as the first half of that corollary.
(2) Lemma 4: added a note that f_y uses the compatible scaling of [6, Lemma 29 / Theorem 39]. Only its zero set is used.
(3) Section 5, p = 5: the printed arc now matches the archived witness arclift_p5_n10.txt, with coordinates stated. The incorrect claim that N = 6 is below the Segre range is replaced: Lemma 4 applies (t = 1); the p >= 30 and p >= 59 thresholds of Theorem 1 fail.
(4) Evidence: lift_opt now returns solver status. arc_search reports 600/600 lifts proved optimal. verify_lemmas separates certified (100/100), inconclusive (0) and counterexample (0) cases for Lemma 3, and reports Lemma 4 only on the 250 (arc, direction) pairs that satisfy its hypotheses. The equality point sets (8 files) and the c > 2 CP-SAT outputs are archived in the supplement.
(5) Section 6: the short-window statement now reads m <= (p-2)/9, i.e. asymptotically n <= 10p/9.
(6) New Section 5: Lemma 7 (pair lemma) and Proposition 8, a closed bound 2n - c_x - c_y - (p-1) for one hyperbola in a window of any side n >= p. Consequences: short windows (n < 2p) never beat 3/2 for a hyperbola, which resolves that open case for hyperbolas; the 2p <= n <= 3p envelope 3(p-1)+2r of [11] is recovered; |S| < 1.8n for n < 5p. Exhaustive checks are in pair_bound_check.c and pair_lemma.py. The concurrent forum certificate [11] is credited.
(7) Section 7, open item 1, now reports that general arcs do beat 3/2 in short windows at small p (12 points at p=5, n=7; 16 at p=7, n=10; both proved optimal), with the p=11 data and the corner-box full-lift mechanism.
Sections renumbered 5 to 8. No change to Theorem 1 or its proof.
title: No arc modulo p beats density 3/2 in the Hall–Jackson–Sudbery–Wild window
